sec-bot: automated scanner detected a file named 'service_account.json' inside GitHub Actions artifact for repo platform/redis-proxy (run id: 11234) — artifact path: actions/artifacts/11234/service_account.json

Ava (sec-eng): 1) Is this from a workflow that uploads artifacts by default? 2) Can we confirm which SA/key it is?

Ben (infra): Looks like the workflow archives test artifacts from the integration test job. Artifact URL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/actions/runs/11234/artifacts/987
Found JSON snippet (sanitized):
```json
{
  "type": "service_account",
  "project_id": "redwood-staging",
  "client_email": "deploy-bot@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com",
  "private_key_id": "abcd1234..."
}
```

Carmen (sre): Confirmed client_email. That SA has limited perms (storage.admin, logs.writer). Need immediate containment.

Ava (sec-eng): Action plan: 1) Revoke the key immediately, 2) Rotate credentials and update deployments, 3) Delete artifact, 4) Run retrospective scan across actions artifacts & recent logs, 5) Add artifact retention/denylist rule.

Dylan (platform): On it. Revoke command I'm running now: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete abcd1234 --iam-account=deploy-bot@redwood-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-staging`

Ben (infra): After revocation, we should restrict the SA IAM bindings — remove storage.admin, grant more granular roles (storage.objectAdmin on bucket only). @Dylan can you file a quick RBAC change?

Dylan (platform): Filing PR and policy: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/498 — will remove broad roles and add specific resource-level grants.

Erin (legal): Note: need to check if artifact was publicly accessible or shared externally. If yes, we have disclosure requirements. Who can confirm access logs?

Carmen (sre): Checking artifact ACLs now. Early result: artifact was private to org, but Actions artifacts can be downloaded by anyone with repo read. No external downloads in the timeframe per audit logs.

Ava (sec-eng): Still treat as sensitive. Post-incident tasks: - rotate any tokens that may have been derived - add KMS encryption for artifact store - add scanning step in workflows to fail on SA JSON or long-looking keys - update runbook to include artifact purge script.

Ben (infra): Implementing KMS envelope encryption for artifact storage: I'll add a middleware to maven/zip upload step to encrypt with projects/redwood-kms/locations/us/keyRings/actions/cryptoKeys/artifacts-key.

Dylan (platform): Quick containment checklist completed: key revoked (see gcloud output), artifact deleted from actions, PR for RBAC opened, running org-wide artifact scan job now (`./scripts/scan-actions-artifacts --since=30d`).

sec-bot: scan job started (job id 20260320-1) — will post results.

Ava (sec-eng): Also schedule a short canary to ensure deploy pipeline still works after credential changes. If anything breaks, fallback to manual deploy runbook.

Erin (legal): Please add a timeline and affected services list to the incident doc. I'll review for any regulatory impact.

Carmen (sre): Found 2 more artifacts in other repos containing short-lived test tokens (all now deleted). No evidence of exfiltration. Will include details in incident doc.

Ava (sec-eng): Post-incident actions assigned: 1) infra: implement artifact KMS + retention policy (Ben), 2) platform: RBAC PR & runbook update (Dylan), 3) sec: add workflow scanner + alerting (Ava), 4) sre: retrospective artifact scan + report (Carmen), 5) legal: compliance review (Erin).

Ben (infra): ETA for infra changes: config + rollout by EOD tomorrow.

Dylan (platform): Runbook PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/502 — includes purge script and rollback notes.

Ava (sec-eng): Thanks team. Will draft incident summary & short postmortem after the scan results. For now treat this as contained. :white_check_mark:
